items.title: Add web_search tool (no URL needed)
items.why: Open questions (all 3 audit lenses top gap) silently failed - every tool needed a URL.
items.how: anvil.webSearch via Bing HTML + unwrapBingUrl; agent web_search tool; system prompt use-first.

items.title: Stream progress on long errands
items.why: Handler goes silent 30-60s during multi-step browse; new user thinks bot is dead and gives up.
items.how: Send an interim working-on-it message when the agent takes >1 browse step or after N seconds.

items.title: Alerts compare extracted value not raw LLM prose
items.why: watch-alerts false-ping on wording drift or miss real moves (firstNumber grabs wrong number).
items.how: Extract a normalized value (number/text) to compare, not the free-text reply; fix firstNumber.

items.title: Atomic store writes (temp+rename)
items.why: Non-atomic writeFileSync + load-empty-on-parse-error = a crash mid-write silently wipes saved reminders/recipes/alerts.
items.how: Write tmp then rename; on load parse-error back up the corrupt file instead of starting empty.

items.title: Fire daily schedules in the user timezone
items.why: nextDailyMs uses server-local setHours; on a UTC VM every-morning-9am fires at 9am UTC = middle of night.
items.how: Capture a per-chat TZ/offset and compute next-daily in it; default RELAY_TZ.

items.title: Mark truncated tool output
items.why: scrape/read/fetch_json silently sliced to 6000 chars; agent answered confidently from the top + missed data below.
items.how: truncateForModel() appends a visible [truncated N more...] marker so the model hedges/re-fetches.

items.title: Per-user profile: home location + units
items.why: 'near me' + bare 'weather' run location-less searches -> generic/wrong results; README even advertises 'best sushi near me'. Unanimous A+C.
items.how: Small per-chat JSON profile store (location, units, tz); a /setlocation or set-my-location flow; agent gets it as context. Ties into the tz work already done.

items.title: Parameterized recipes with slots
items.why: Recipes store a fixed task string; a user must re-teach per item. Slots turn one taught recipe into a reusable tool.
items.how: Parse {slot} in recipe task; /run <name> <value> substitutes. recipes.ts parser change + handler run-path.

items.title: Absolute-threshold + back-in-stock alerts
items.why: Alerts only do 'changed by N'; users think in 'below 50k' / 'back in stock'. Extends the most retention-driving feature.
items.how: Parse a comparison operator (below/above/back in stock) in the watch command; alert-runner evaluates the predicate vs extractValue/text.

items.title: Accept inbound photos (vision)
items.why: Image-only messages get rejected ('send a task in words'); texting a photo (menu/receipt/product) is a natural first move + the biggest input gap vs Instinct. A+C.
items.how: Download Telegram photo file_id, pass bytes to Gemini (already multimodal) as an image part; handler accepts media messages. Free (Gemini free tier is multimodal).

items.title: Thread profile location into proactive runs
items.why: Scheduled 'weather'/'near me' digests+recipes+alerts dropped the profileContext the inbound path injects -> every location-based daily silently wrong.
items.how: contextFor(chatId) dep on schedule/digest/alert runners -> runAgent({llm,context}); index wires profiles.contextLine.

items.title: Mark truncation in extractOne (extract/compare/alerts)
items.why: extract/compare/alerts read content.slice(0,8000) with no marker -> a value below the cut is silently missed + reported as fact.
items.how: Apply truncateForModel (already exists) to the content passed to extractFieldsResult in extractOne.

items.title: Reject empty-arg on a slotted recipe
items.why: '/run track' on 'price of {item}' substitutes empty -> runs a broken task + confident nonsense.
items.how: If a recipe task has {slots} but args is empty, reply asking for the value instead of running. applySlots/handler run-path.

items.title: Accept inbound voice notes (transcribe + run)
items.why: Voice message = zero reply (dropped like non-photo media); voice-texting is a top interaction + Instinct's headline. Unanimous A+C.
items.how: parseUpdates emits voice file_id; downloadFile bytes; Gemini audio transcription (free multimodal) -> run as a normal task. Mirror the photo path.

items.title: Understand forwarded documents/PDFs
items.why: Forwarding a PDF/statement + 'summarize this' is dropped; asymmetric (bot sends PDFs, can't receive). A+C.
items.how: parseUpdates emits document file_id; downloadFile; Gemini reads PDF bytes (multimodal) -> answer. Mirror photo path.

items.title: Refuse scheduling a slotted recipe
items.why: recipeSchedule stored rec.task raw, so 'schedule track every morning' on 'price of {item}' fired literal {item} daily = confident nonsense.
items.how: hasSlots check in recipeSchedule -> reason 'needsarg'; handler explains it can't run on a schedule with a fixed value.

items.title: Derive per-user timezone from location profile
items.why: Profile stores a city but daily schedules use one global RELAY_TZ_OFFSET_MIN, so an Austin user's 'every morning 9am' fires at 9am UTC = 3-4am. A+B.
items.how: Add optional tzOffsetMin to Profile; scheduler/nextDailyMs uses the chat's offset when set (fall back to global). Best-effort derive from location via a static city->offset map or a set-timezone command; at minimum let user set it.

items.title: Run an alert check immediately on define
items.why: 'watch btc below 50000' first checks at the default 09:00 cadence -> up to ~24h silence even if already true; user thinks it's broken.
items.how: After alertDefine, run checkAlert once now (baseline + notify if the predicate already holds), like the inbound /run alert path.

items.title: Stop extractValue tracking a % / rating over the price
items.why: extractValue prefers the first decimal, so 'BTC up 2.5% at 68000' tracks 2.5 -> 'below 50000' always fires, 'above 70000' never. Breaks predicate alerts.
items.how: Prefer a currency-tagged or largest-magnitude number over a %/small decimal; ignore numbers immediately followed by % when a bigger bare number exists.

items.title: Persist the user turn on the agent-error path
items.why: On runAgent throw the handler sends friendlyError but never memorySet, so a follow-up ('why did that fail? try again') has zero context.
items.how: In the handler catch, record the user message (+ a brief note the attempt failed) to memory so the next turn is coherent.

items.title: Change-alerts compare against the last NOTIFIED value, not last observed
items.why: checkAlert calls setLast on EVERY check, so a 'by 1000' watch resets its baseline to the newest value each time; BTC drifting 65000->66200 in three <1000 steps never fires. Core threshold promise silently broken (audit 5 B#1).
items.how: For the change (threshold) path, only advance lastValue when it actually notifies (or on first run); keep the last-notified value as the comparison baseline so cumulative drift is measured.

items.title: Greet + show intro on 'hi'/'what can you do', not just /start
items.why: Onboarding fires only on the literal /start command a new user doesn't know; 'hi'/'hey'/'what can you do?' get run as a browser task -> wasted first message, user bounces (audit 5 A#1).
items.how: Detect a bare greeting / capability question in the handler (before the agent) and reply with the /start intro. Keep it tight so it doesn't swallow real tasks.

items.title: Don't re-fire a predicate alert after a transient numberless check
items.why: A real-but-numberless reply ('price unavailable') isn't degraded, so it's stored as lastValue; next check prevHolds=null and the edge test re-fires 'below 50k' though it never left the below state -> spurious double-ping trains users to ignore alerts (audit 5 B#5).
items.how: In checkAlert's predicate path, if the new value has no comparable value (conditionHolds indeterminate / extractValue null for below-above), skip setLast + skip notify (like the degraded guard) so the last GOOD value stays the baseline.

items.title: Edit a saved recipe/digest/alert by talking to it
items.why: To change a digest time or an alert threshold a user must delete + recreate; the parse layers already exist, so an edit path is cheap and grows how many automations a user keeps alive (audit 5 C#4).
items.how: Parse an edit intent ('change my morning digest to 7am', 'make that alert fire under 200') -> find by name -> update the stored item in place via the existing stores. Start with the highest-value field (schedule time / threshold).

items.title: Skip (or flag) an unfilled {slot} recipe inside a digest
items.why: runDigest hands rec.task straight to runAgent with no hasSlots check (unlike /run + schedule which guard it), so a digest member like 'track price of {item}' runs the literal broken task and silently poisons the briefing the user reads as authoritative (audit 6 B#3).
items.how: In digest-runner, hasSlots(member.task) -> skip it with a one-line 'skipped <name> (needs a value)' note in the composed briefing instead of running the broken task.

items.title: Split long replies instead of silently truncating at 4096
items.why: telegram.ts sendMessage does text.slice(0,4096) with no marker, so a long digest/answer is cut mid-sentence and the user reads a partial result believing it's complete (audit 6 B#4).
items.how: Chunk a >4096-char message on paragraph/line boundaries into sequential sends (Telegram max 4096), or at minimum append a visible '…(continued)'/'[truncated]' marker. Prefer real multi-message send.

items.title: Stop non-numeric alerts false-firing on prose drift
items.why: changed() falls back to raw trimmed-text inequality when neither side is numeric, so a 'watch top HN story' style alert pings 'changed' nearly every check because the agent's wording varies run-to-run even when the answer is the same -> alert spam, user tunes it out (audit 6 B#2).
items.how: Normalize the compared text (lowercase, collapse whitespace/punctuation) and/or extract a salient token; only fire when the meaningful content differs, not incidental phrasing. Consider asking the LLM for a stable one-line key for the watched thing.

items.title: Ask one clarifying question before an ambiguous first errand
items.why: A vague opener ('find me a good laptop', 'cheap flights to Lisbon') runs immediately against guessed sites/params, spending the highest-leverage first message on a guess the user didn't ask for (audit 6 A#3).
items.how: Detect a genuinely underspecified task (missing dates/budget/target) and ask ONE targeted question before running; keep it rare so it doesn't nag on clear tasks. Likely a light heuristic + a system-prompt nudge.

items.title: Dangerous-action guard shouldn't match the TYPED text
items.why: agent.ts builds the guard label as label+selector+TYPED-text, so typing a query with a trigger word ('search Goodreads for this book', 'cancel culture', 'order status') is REFUSED as a committing action -> a whole class of normal browsing silently dead-ends with a scary refusal. Flagged 3 audits running (7 B#1, 6, 5).
items.how: Guard the click TARGET only (label + selector) — typing into a field isn't the committing act, the click/submit is. Drop call.args.text from the isDangerousAction() label in the type/click branch. Keep refusing a click whose label/selector says pay/submit/delete.

items.title: Don't silently delete a once-reminder that hits the hourly cap
items.why: schedule-runner over-cap path safeComplete()s a due 'once' reminder with no send + no failureNotice, so 'remind me to take my meds at 3pm' during a busy hour is deleted forever with only a log line — the highest-trust promise, a black hole (audit 7 B#2, 6 B).
items.how: In the runner tick, when a DUE once-reminder is over the proactive cap, DON'T complete it — defer (leave dueMs or bump slightly) so it fires next tick, or send it anyway (a one-shot the user explicitly set isn't spam). Dailies keep the cap. Add a test for defer-not-drop.

items.title: Register the Telegram slash-command menu (setMyCommands)
items.why: No setMyCommands call exists, so Telegram's native '/' autocomplete is empty; the 12 commands are a bare wall of names in /start with no descriptions -> a new user can't discover or correctly type /run, /alerts, /setlocation in the first 10 min (audit 7 A#4).
items.how: On startup call the Bot API setMyCommands with each command + a one-line description (reuse the Commands: list). One HTTP call in telegram.ts, invoked from index main(). Keep it best-effort (log on failure).

items.title: Answer calc/convert/known-fact instantly, no browser round-trip
items.why: '20% tip on $47', '100 USD in EUR', 'oz in a cup', 'capital of France' trigger a slow web_search/scrape (or risk the 'never invent data' refusal), adding 10-30s to the exact throwaway questions people first test the bot with (audit 7 A#5).
items.how: Let the agent answer directly (reply without a tool) for arithmetic/unit-conversion/common-knowledge that needs no live data; a SYSTEM_PROMPT carve-out to the 'never invent data' rule for deterministic math/facts. Keep web_search for anything time-sensitive or uncertain.

items.title: "I'm in X" location-setter hijacks normal messages + reminders
items.why: parseSetLocation's `i'm in (.+)` matches ANY conversational 'I'm in ...' and runs before schedule-parse + the agent, so 'I'm in a meeting, remind me in 10 min' is swallowed: reminder never scheduled, no answer, and 'a meeting, remind me...' saved as home location -> corrupts every future weather/near-me (audit 8 B#1).
items.how: Tighten the 'i'm in' branch: only treat it as a location-set when the tail looks like a place (short, no comma-clause with a verb, no scheduling words like remind/in N min/every). Prefer the explicit '/setlocation' + 'set my location to' forms; make bare 'I'm in X' require X to be a plausible place (1-4 words, no trailing task clause). Add tests for the false-positives.

items.title: Threshold change-alert shouldn't fire/poison baseline on a numberless check
items.why: checkAlert guards the indeterminate case only for PREDICATE alerts; the threshold/plain-change path has no equivalent, so a transient numberless reply ('price unavailable') makes changed() fall back to text-diff, false-pings '🔔 changed', and stores the non-numeric string as baseline -> the 'by N' threshold is silently bypassed across the gap (audit 8 B#2).
items.how: In checkAlert's non-predicate path, if the alert has a numeric threshold and extractValue(newValue) is null, skip notify + skip setLast (keep last good baseline), mirroring the predicate-refire-guard + the degraded guard.

items.title: Run a check after editing an alert into an already-true predicate
items.why: The define path runs alertRunNow to catch an already-satisfied predicate, but alertEdit just updates + returns; 'change btc to below 55000' when BTC is already below confirms 'Updated...' then never pings (no edge vs the preserved lastValue) -> user waits for a fire that may never come (audit 8 B#4).
items.how: After a successful alertEdit, run alertRunNow(chatId, name) like the define path and relay the message if it fires. Reset the baseline so the edited predicate edge-triggers correctly.

items.title: View / clear your saved profile over text
items.why: After /setlocation a user can't see or correct what was stored; a typo'd 'UTC-5' or wrong city is invisible + silently wrong on every weather/near-me/daily reminder (audit 8 A#2).
items.how: Add a /profile (or 'what's my location') read that echoes stored location/units/tz, and a clear/forget path. Handler branch + ProfileStore already has get; add a clear.

items.title: NL scheduler hijacks watch/save/digest commands containing a cadence word
items.why: The schedule keyword-regex ran before the alert/save/digest define branches, guarded only against slash + run/schedule verbs; 'watch daily: btc' / 'save morning-brief: ...' contains a cadence word so it got turned into a reminder + the alert/recipe/digest was never created (audit 9 B#1).
items.how: Extend the guard to skip messages matching a define shape ('<watch|alert me|save|[define] digest> <name>: <task>') or an alert-edit shape ('<change|set|make> ... <below|above|in stock|by>'); match the SHAPE not just the verb so 'set a reminder every day' still schedules.

items.title: Re-queue a once-reminder that fails at fire time, not delete it
items.why: schedule-runner's fireOne catch always safeComplete()s a 'once' on ANY throw, so 'remind me to take my meds at 3pm' vanishes on a momentary anvil/LLM hiccup at 3pm — only the rate-cap path defers (audit 9 B#2, also 8 B).
items.how: On a fireOne failure for a 'once', don't complete — defer for a bounded number of retries (e.g. keep it due, track an attempt count, drop after N so a permanently-broken task doesn't loop forever). Daily still advances. Send the failure notice only after the retries exhaust.

items.title: Weekly / weekday / interval reminders
items.why: schedule.ts parses only once + daily; 'every Monday', 'weekdays at 8', 'every 2 hours' silently fall through to a one-off agent run that does nothing — a core recurring-reminder shape fails on first try (audit 9 A#2).
items.how: Extend parseSchedule + Schedule kind to support day-of-week ('every monday'), weekday/weekend, and sub-daily intervals ('every N hours'); complete() advances to the next matching occurrence. New ScheduleKind values + nextOccurrence logic + tests.

items.title: Offer to save a repeated ask as a recipe/alert
items.why: Recipes/alerts exist but users must know the 'save X:' syntax; most never do, so the retention flywheel never starts. Detecting a repeated ask + proposing the save+schedule converts casual use into the sticky proactive loop (audit 9 C#1).
items.how: On an inbound task that closely matches a recent one (per-chat memory), append a one-line 'want me to save this as a recipe / check it every morning?' nudge to the reply. Light similarity check; no new infra (reuse memory-store + recipes).

history.event: PRODUCT-LOOP iter 1: bootstrapped backlog via 3-agent parallel audit; web_search TOP in all 3 lenses -> built it. anvil.webSearch (Bing HTML + unwrapBingUrl; DDG html+lite CAPTCHA a headless Chrome, Bing does not), agent web_search tool + system-prompt use-first, optional BrowserBackend.webSearch. +8 tests. 574 pass, tsc clean. LIVE-VERIFIED: real Bing results unwrapped to clean https (wikipedia/britannica) 5/5. Seeded 4 more high-impact todos.

PRODUCT-LOOP iter 2: built progress-ping (audit A#2, top impact/effort). Handler arms a one-shot timer around the agent run; if it outlasts progressDelayMs (default 6s, RELAY_PROGRESS_DELAY_MS, 0 disables) it sends ONE 'Still working on it - reading the web, hang tight...' then the reply; timer cleared on success AND error. Injectable setTimer/clearTimer for offline tests. So a 30-60s multi-step browse no longer reads as a dead bot. +3 handler tests (ping-then-reply, no-ping-when-unset, cleared-on-error). 577 pass, tsc clean. call-tested false (UX-timer wiring, unit-tested via injected timer). Remaining todos: alert-value-compare, atomic-store-writes, tz-daily-schedules.

PRODUCT-LOOP iter 3: built alert-value-compare (audit B, core proactive-promise fix). changed() now compares the SALIENT VALUE via new extractValue() (currency-tagged > decimal > largest-magnitude) instead of raw LLM prose + firstNumber (which grabbed a date/count). So a watch-alert no longer false-pings when wording drifts run-to-run but the tracked price is identical, and a real move still fires. Non-numeric watches (in-stock/sold-out) fall back to text-diff. firstNumber kept (signature unchanged). +8 tests incl the drift-same-value + incidental-date cases. 584 pass, tsc clean. call-tested false (pure compare logic, exhaustively unit-tested). Remaining: atomic-store-writes, tz-daily-schedules.

PRODUCT-LOOP iter 4: built atomic-store-writes (audit B, highest-severity data-loss). New src/lib/safe-store.ts: atomicWriteJson (mkdir+write .tmp+rename = atomic, reader sees old-or-new never torn; cleans .tmp on failed rename; never throws) + readJsonSafe (missing->null; CORRUPT->move to .corrupt then null, instead of silently wiping). Applied to all 5 stores (schedule/recipes/digests/alerts/memory) — replaced their bare writeFileSync + catch-set-empty. So a crash mid-write or one corrupt byte no longer vanishes every saved reminder/recipe/alert; corrupt data is preserved for recovery. +8 safe-store tests (round-trip, mkdir, no-tmp-leak, no-throw-unwritable, corrupt-backup, torn-tmp-not-live); all 5 stores existing tests still green (behavior-preserving). 592 pass, tsc clean. call-tested false (fs-level, unit-tested incl crash-sim). Remaining: tz-daily-schedules (last todo -> audit refills next).

PRODUCT-LOOP iter 5: built tz-daily-schedules (audit B). nextDailyMs was server-local setHours -> on a UTC VM 'every morning 9am' fired at 9am UTC (middle of night). Rewrote it to compute purely from UTC + a tz offset (tzOffsetMin from RELAY_TZ_OFFSET_MIN, minutes east of UTC, default 0=UTC, back-compat); exported nextDailyMs+tzOffsetMin. Updated 3 schedule tests to assert host-independently (getUTCHours) + added a tz-offset test (UTC/US-Eastern/CET wall-clock + tomorrow-rollover). Added RELAY_TZ_OFFSET_MIN to .env.example. 594 pass, tsc clean. call-tested false (pure time math, unit-tested). Backlog now DRY -> running 3-agent audit to refill (same iteration).
